plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs covered in rose-like blooms with layered, silky petals and golden centers. They bring bright color to the quiet days of midwinter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring, with a peak in winter in mild climates
plants.location: Southern Japan, the Pacific Northwest of the United States and the southeastern United States
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Japanese gardeners have cultivated it for centuries, and thousands of cultivars now exist.

plants.name: Delosperma cooperi
plants.description: A sprawling, succulent groundcover whose daisy-like flowers shimmer in the summer sun. The petals are narrow and glistening, and they open in dazzling magenta carpets.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer, roughly November to March
plants.location: Eastern South Africa, including the Drakensberg foothills and Eastern Cape
plants.funFact: The glistening look comes from tiny bladder-like cells on the leaves and petals that store water. They help the plant survive dry spells.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima
plants.description: A bold crimson flower head ringed with leafy bracts, standing tall on the shrub. Nectar-seeking birds are drawn to it across the bushland of southeastern Australia.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring, around September to November, with the flowers mostly finished by January
plants.location: Sydney sandstone region, New South Wales, Australia
plants.funFact: The waratah is the floral emblem of New South Wales. Each flower head is made up of hundreds of tiny individual flowers.
